study_identification_part.si4_title: Individual-level deviations from normative brain morphology in violence, psychosis, and psychopathy

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Normative models based on large lifespan reference data were used to map individual-level deviations in cortical thickness, surface area, and subcortical volumes among men with schizophrenia spectrum disorders with and without a history of severe violence and violent men without schizophrenia, and to test group differences and associations with psychopathy traits.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The reference normative models are described as pretrained (BrainCharts GitHub) and trained on 82 sites but specific dataset names are not listed.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: We used pretrained normative models from https://github.com/predictiveclinical-neuroscience/braincharts. ... models were trained using data of 58835 individuals ... from 82 sites.

rci2_hc_n.reason: The paper and Table 1 clearly state the number of healthy controls in the analysis group.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: healthy controls (HC, n = 196) matched by age and scanner.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Heterogeneous individual deviation patterns across groups; SSD-V showed elevated extreme negative deviations particularly in collateral transverse sulcus, lingual gyrus, and cerebellum; SSD-NV and nonSSD-V showed distinct regional patterns; no significant associations with psychopathy after multiple-comparison correction.
